key_insight: An NLP ensemble identified brain metastases in radiology reports, supporting cancer surveillance rather than drug discovery.
clinical_relevance: The pipeline could help cancer registries capture brain metastases arising after initial cancer diagnosis that current surveillance may miss.
method: Manually labeled brain/head radiology reports from a population-based Alberta cancer cohort.
Trained separate Bio_ClinicalBERT models on Findings and Impressions sections.
Used the higher section-level probability as the report prediction and validated across three Canadian provinces.
evidence_signal: Trained on 1,879 samples, the ensemble achieved 88.8% sensitivity and 49.9% precision on 1,833 internal-validation reports from 357 patients at a 0.4 threshold; external sensitivity was 91.8% in Ontario and 72.6% in British Columbia.
watch_item: Modest internal precision and variable external sensitivity warrant local validation and review workflows before registry implementation.
paper_title: Natural Language Processing Based Solution for Labeling Brain Metastasis Identified in Radiology Reports
